title: LG Innotek's AI Accelerator Substrate Enters Customer Validation, Eyes 2027 Mass Production
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 2, 2026

LG Innotek's AI accelerator FC-BGA substrate has entered customer validation, putting the company on track for 2027 mass production in a high-end chip-packaging segment long dominated by Samsung Electro-Mechanics. Here's what's been disclosed about the product and the business behind it.

CompanyRoleEvidence
LG Innotek
KRX: 011070		Developing AI accelerator-grade FC-BGA substrates, now in customer validationReported: exclusive report citing company sources, Oct 2, 2026

What's been disclosed

  • Customer validation underway: LG Innotek's AI accelerator-focused FC-BGA (flip-chip ball grid array) substrates have moved into customer validation, targeting 2027 mass production.
  • Product already shown publicly: The company unveiled large-format (100mm-plus) AI accelerator FC-BGA boards at the KPCA Show 2026 trade show last month.
  • Business build-up: LG Innotek entered the FC-BGA market in 2022 with network/modem and TV applications, added PC chipset supply for global tech customers in 2024, expanded into CPU applications in Q3 2026, and is now targeting AI accelerators with a broader goal of competing in the high-end FC-BGA market by 2028.
  • Segment financials: The company's package solutions division posted 935.6 billion won in revenue (+18% year-over-year) and 99.6 billion won in operating profit (+94% year-over-year) in H1 2026, with a stated target of 1 trillion won in annual operating profit by 2031.
  • Late entrant, fast escalation: LG Innotek entered the FC-BGA market more than a decade after Samsung Electro-Mechanics but has rapidly moved up the product ladder, now pushing into high-specification segments — AI training/inference, autonomous vehicles, and servers — that Samsung Electro-Mechanics has long led.
  • Company statement: LG Innotek said AI accelerator FC-BGA products are targeted for 2027 mass production, with customer discussions and supply implementation work ongoing.

Why this matters

FC-BGA substrates are a key bottleneck component for advanced AI chips, sitting between the chip itself and the circuit board and requiring extreme precision at large panel sizes. The segment has historically been the domain of a small number of Japanese and Korean suppliers, with Samsung Electro-Mechanics as Korea's dominant player. A credible second domestic entrant at the AI-accelerator tier would diversify the supply base for Korean and global chipmakers relying on advanced packaging. (Reported)

What's still unconfirmed

No customer names were disclosed, nor was pricing, initial production volume, or which specific AI accelerator chips the substrates are being validated against. Whether LG Innotek can close the technology and yield gap with Samsung Electro-Mechanics at the most advanced specifications by 2027 is also not yet established. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

What is an FC-BGA substrate and why does it matter for AI chips?
It's the substrate that connects an advanced chip (like an AI accelerator) to the circuit board. At large sizes and high layer counts, it's difficult to manufacture and is considered a bottleneck component for high-end AI hardware.

Is LG Innotek already making these for customers?
Not yet in mass production. The company is in the "customer validation" stage, which precedes mass production, targeted for 2027.

How does this compare to Samsung Electro-Mechanics?
Samsung Electro-Mechanics has led Korea's FC-BGA market for AI/server-grade substrates for years. LG Innotek entered the broader FC-BGA market more than a decade later and is now pushing into this top-tier segment, per the company's own disclosed roadmap.
